description: The JWT token containing the unique identifier is transmitted in the data flow, potentially exposing the identifier to interception or monitoring.
assumptions: JWTs are transmitted as part of the authentication flow and contain identifying information.

title: Sensitive data stored in localStorage
description: JWT tokens are sensitive authentication data that should be stored securely, but localStorage is exposed to the browser and can be accessed by malicious scripts.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to JavaScript and can be read by malicious scripts or extensions.

title: Data accessible to more parties than necessary
description: localStorage exposes JWT tokens to all scripts running in the browser, including potentially malicious third-party scripts or extensions.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to all scripts in the browser context, not just the originating application.

title: User unaware of JWT storage
description: Users may not be aware that their JWT tokens are being stored in localStorage, which could be accessed by malicious actors.
assumptions: Users typically do not understand the implications of localStorage storage for authentication tokens.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing JWT tokens in localStorage may violate data minimization principles as the data is stored longer than functionally needed and in a less secure location than necessary.
assumptions: JWT tokens should be stored in a more secure location (e.g., httpOnly cookies) rather than localStorage.

title: Child history data linked through unique identifiers
description: Child history data retrieved from P3 may contain unique identifiers (e.g., child ID, name, DOB) that can be used to link the child to other data sources or databases.

title: Child history data linked through quasi-identifier combination
description: Child history data may contain multiple quasi-identifiers (e.g., age, school, location) that can be combined to identify the child.

title: Processing of identified child history data
description: The source process P3 processes identified data (child history) which may contain personal information about the child.

title: Child history contains unique references to identity
description: The child history data contains unique references to the child's identity that can be used to identify the data subject.

title: Child history data type sensitivity exceeds functional requirement
description: Child history data may be more sensitive than functionally required for the parent review purpose.

title: Child history disclosed to predetermined set of parties
description: Child history is disclosed only to the parent (predetermined set), but this may exceed what is functionally necessary for the review purpose.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Child history data may be processed in excess of what is actually needed for the parent review function.

title: Data flow meta-data may link parties
description: The data flow DF17 itself may contain meta-data (e.g., timestamps, source/destination identifiers) that can be used to link the parent to the child.

title: Communication metadata involves identified information
description: The metadata of the data flow may involve identified information about the parties involved in the communication.

title: Parent system response may reveal child information
description: The parent's system response to the child history retrieval may reveal information about the child's existence or data processing.

title: Parent may analyze data beyond functional need
description: The parent may analyze or process the child history data in ways that exceed the functional requirements of the review purpose.
